summary.headline: Harsha Engineers Q1 FY27 consolidated Engineering supply up 25% YoY to Rs 421 crore, but EBITDA margin compressed on a 6-7% raw material spike pending pass-through.
summary.overview: Consolidated Engineering supply rose to Rs 421 crore from Rs 382 crore QoQ and Rs 349 crore YoY, with India Engineering growing about 21% YoY and 6% QoQ. Consolidated Engineering EBITDA was Rs 69.8 crore versus Rs 77 crore QoQ and Rs 65.3 crore YoY, so margin fell QoQ. Management attributed the squeeze to an ~8% rise in average raw material cost (lagged pass-through of one to two quarters), about Rs 4 crore of FX hedge accounting loss, and about Rs 3 crore of higher indirect material costs after the West Asia conflict. Management kept FY27 guidance of high-teens India growth and low-teens consolidated growth, with India Engineering EBITDA margin of 22-24%.

segments.name: India Engineering (HEIL + Harsha Advantek)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 21% YoY and 6% QoQ; EBITDA and PAT up YoY but margin down QoQ on material pass-through lag and FX loss. Management guides high-teens India growth for FY27.

segments.name: Harsha Advantek (wholly owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q1 sales about Rs 30 crore (+7% QoQ), EBITDA margin about 9%. FY27 target Rs 140 crore plus vs Rs 43 crore in FY26; expected PAT positive by end-FY27.

segments.name: Harsha China
segments.commentary: Stable and profitable; FY27 revenue growth about 10% on FY26 base of about Rs 120 crore, EBITDA margin 12-14%, PAT about 6%. Brownfield steel cage expansion to commission by Q3 FY28.

segments.name: Harsha Romania
segments.commentary: Still loss-making; slight top-line growth but one-time FX loss of about Rs 2 crore in Q1. Management expects some losses in FY27, aiming for break-even; new top management in place.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs 36.3 crore, EBITDA Rs 2.82 crore; management guides about Rs 200 crore FY27 revenue at 7-8% EBITDA margin, project-driven and seasonal.

segments.name: Large-size cages
segments.commentary: Q1 sales only about Rs 10 crore on capacity ramp-up constraints at new facility; management still targets about 50% growth on FY26 base of Rs 49 crore (the call also cites about 30%, so the target is unclear).

guidance_outlook: India Engineering: high-teens growth in FY27 (volume-led, with some price pass-through); India Engineering EBITDA margin guided at 22-24%, with management noting the 24% Q1 standalone figure may be high due to lag cycles.
Consolidated FY27: low-to-mid-teens sales growth; management called 20% a very tough stretch.
Bushing: about 30% growth in FY27 vs Rs 127 crore in FY26.
Stamping: about 30% growth in FY27 vs Rs 60 crore in FY26.
Japanese customers: about 10% growth to about Rs 72-80 crore (management also said Rs 80 crore or thereabouts).
Consolidated EBITDA margin could recover to about 18% (FY26 level 18.7%) if metal prices stabilise; management had no view on RM price normalisation.
Subsidiaries: China plus Romania revenue growth below 10%; combined FY27 loss about Rs 2-3 crore, with Romania possibly profitable next year.
CapEx: Rs 50-80 crore per year, with Rs 180-200 crore combined over 1.5-2 years for Bhayla Phase-2 and China expansion.
capex_capacity: Bhayla (India) Phase-2 expansion: building construction delayed by heavy rain in Ahmedabad, expected to start this month; third building targeted for completion by end-2026 or Q4 FY27.
Bhayla total target: about Rs 300-400 crore revenue by year three across both phases; Phase-1 and Phase-2 demand visibility expected to absorb capacity within about one year.
China Brownfield steel cage expansion: funded with debt at attractive rate; construction under way; commissioning around Q3 FY28; full impact from FY29.
Large-size cage capacity at new facility still ramping up, constraining Q1 volumes.
Advantek Phase-2 expansion (bushings, stampings, large cages) announced earlier; Advantek FY27 target Rs 140 crore plus.
demand_pricing: Cage demand strong in India from bearing majors and MNC customers' new plants; exports from India Rs 139 crore, +22% YoY.
Europe and US demand improving alongside industrial demand; management described growth as broad-based.
Raw material cost up about 8% in Q1 across brass, copper, zinc, steel and polymer; pass-through lag of one to two quarters (about four months per CFO).
Management estimated the raw material increase would lift prices by about 3-4% (CFO said 40-50% of a 6-7% increase), though the CEO declined to quantify the price impact.
Top 10 customers about 80% of revenue; top customers (SKF, Schaeffler, Timken, NBC, ZF, Flender) rank in a shifting order; management claims 80-90% wallet share with major Indian customers.
Management cited wind bushing upgrades, rail stampings and defence/aerospace stamping developments as future growth areas.

qa_highlights.question: Was the growth broad-based across segments, and was it driven by Europe or India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was broad-based, with industrial demand strengthening in India and European demand recovering. It called 20% FY27 consolidated growth a very tough stretch and expects mid-to-high-teens India growth and low-teens consolidated growth.

qa_highlights.question: Which raw materials drove the cost increase, and how is foreign EBITDA margin trending?
qa_highlights.answer: The RM increase spans brass, copper, zinc, steel and polymer, not just brass as last year. On foreign subsidiaries, management said it is trying to shift to cages, while the raw material spike and FX offset the revenue gains. Management did not quantify the margin decline.

qa_highlights.question: How large are the Romania losses, and is the subsidiary restructuring on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Romania did not significantly improve ex-FX and copper prices hurt results. Sanjay Majmudar guided combined China and Romania loss of about Rs 2-3 crore for FY27 versus about Rs 10 crore last year, with Romania possibly profitable next year.

qa_highlights.question: Are bushing and stamping growth sustainable, and is large-cage growth credible after a weak Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Bushing growth is driven by conversion and wallet share, with conversion expected to support growth for at least a couple of years. Stamping growth comes from new products maturing over about one year. Large-cage Q1 was about Rs 10 crore due to ramp-up constraints at the new facility, and management still expects about 30-50% growth, citing order book and pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CapEx outlook for FY27 and FY28, and what is the Bhayla status?
qa_highlights.answer: China Phase-2 is on track for Q3 FY28 commissioning. Bhayla building construction was delayed by heavy rain and expected to start this month, with the third building targeted for completion by end-2026 or Q4 FY27. Annual CapEx is guided at Rs 50-80 crore, with Rs 180-200 crore over 1.5-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: How much of India growth is volume versus price, and what price increase is being taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth is the focus and the price impact is not being predicted. Maulik Jasani estimated the 6-7% RM increase would lift selling prices by about 40-50% of that, roughly 3-4%. The Japanese customer was Rs 21 crore in Q1 versus Rs 16.5 crore a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Advantek EBITDA and margin expectations, and what is the normal India Engineering margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Advantek Q1 EBITDA margin was about 9%, and it is expected to be slightly below the India blended margin in FY27, matching it from FY28. Vishal Rangwala said the 24% Q1 standalone margin is high and a normal sustainable margin is 20-22%. Jason Soans's question on the 22-24% guidance was answered by Maulik Jasani, who said margin percentage will fall as pass-through lifts realisations.

risks_watch: Raw material pass-through lag of one to two quarters: Q1 margin compressed on an 8% RM rise, and recovery depends on metal prices stabilising (management had no view on normalisation).
Solar EPC volatility: Q1 revenue Rs 36.3 crore vs a Q4-heavy seasonal pattern; FY27 guide of about Rs 200 crore at 7-8% EBITDA margin.
Romania: still loss-making, one-time FX loss of about Rs 2 crore in Q1, no break-even timeline, and copper prices weighed on results.
Large-size cages: Q1 sales about Rs 10 crore and new facility still ramping; the FY27 growth target is stated as both about 50% and about 30%, so it needs clarification.
Bhayla Phase-2 construction delayed by monsoon rain, and China commissioning slipped to Q3 FY28 with revenue from FY29; watch construction milestones next quarter.
Advantek PAT-positive target by end-FY27, with FY27 sales target of about Rs 140 crore plus against Rs 43 crore in FY26.
key_quotes: As you would have seen on a consolidated basis, we have posted a 25% growth in Quarter 1 and year-over-year
However, there will be a lag of one or two quarters. Thus, we should be able to pass through this cost increase in the subsequent quarter.
I think 20% is a very tough stretch.
So, we expect that absolute value increase will continue, but definitely percentage will reduce because the material pass through will enhance the sales price recovery
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on demand and growth targets, describing Q1 as satisfactory and in line with plan. It was cautious and often hedged on margins, raw material pass-through, Romania's path to break-even, and the large-cage ramp, and several answers were inconsistent or deferred to later quarters.
